newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended almost unchanged on Thursday after a dull session spent hovering near Wednesday's closing levels and tracking sister markets.
But traders said bonos were starting to tire. Some were looking for a consolidation as long-bond future's move to record highs at 117.17 failed to spark active buying.
"People were expecting the break of 117.05 to act as a buying signal, but although we broke that level the market lacked fuel," a Madrid-based dealer said.
"What I think is that these prices are too high. So we need a correction before starting a new bullish period," he added.
The 10-year spread ended at around 65 basis points unchanged from yesterday, but some dealers said it could correct a bit on Friday in anticipation of next week's Treasury auction.

At the beginning of July, the Spanish Treasury is offering new bonds with different maturities, for its regular monthly refunding. For the first time ever it would offer strippable assets, and this should attract buying interest, they said.
A sliding peseta against the mark, was also adding pressure to bonos, dealers said.
